response.sql: WITH per AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(fillcount) AS a FROM orderexecutions GROUP BY ordersmark), b1 AS (SELECT AVG(a) AS m FROM per WHERE a IS NOT NULL), k1 AS (SELECT a, a - (SELECT m FROM b1) AS e1 FROM per WHERE a > (SELECT m FROM b1)), b2 AS (SELECT AVG(a) AS m FROM k1), k2 AS (SELECT a, e1, a - (SELECT m FROM b2) AS e2 FROM k1 WHERE a > (SELECT m FROM b2)) SELECT AVG(a) AS avg_fill_quantity, AVG(e1) AS avg_first_excess, AVG(e2) AS avg_second_excess FROM k2

assumptions.assumption: Orders are grouped by orderexecutions.ordersmark alone, so executions with a NULL reference form a single group. Per-order averages are not restricted to ordersmark values that exist in orders.
Orders whose fillcount values are all NULL have a NULL average. They are left out of the benchmarks and cannot be kept, because a NULL never passes the 'above' comparison.
'Above' means strictly greater than the benchmark. Orders equal to it are dropped.
